summary: Iteration 11 — Backend-only verification of the image-compression bug fix (blank/oversized wardrobe photos). Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iteration11_image_compression.py (7 tests, class-based pytest). ALL 7 PASSED in 7.6s. Verified: (1) POST /api/items with a real 2400px Unsplash shirt JPEG (746,356 char base64 = 559KB raw) → stored `photo` = 68,484 chars (11x smaller, ~51KB raw), starts with '/9j/4AAQ' JPEG magic and decodes as valid image; GET /api/items/{id} confirms persistence with identical bounded size. (2) POST /api/items also compresses `worn_photo` (same 68,484 output). (3) PUT /api/items/{id} with the same large photo → stored `photo` = 68,484 chars, valid JPEG, persists via GET. (4) POST /api/capture with a small garment JPEG (clean:true) → 200 in 5.6s; analysis populated (name, category, colour, fabric, pattern...); clean_image = 34,424 chars (~26KB raw JPEG), head '/9j/4AAQ' — far below the pre-fix ~460KB baseline. Bounded on first attempt, so retry loop exited immediately. (5) GET /api/items for user_testaura01: 8 items, 3 with photos, 0 oversized (>=250KB base64), 0 invalid — migration + create-path guarantee holds. (6) Regression: name/category/colour round-trip preserved; item appears in list with integer pairs_count (5). (7) Cleanup verified — every TEST_ item DELETED via /api/items/{id}; Mongo direct query confirms no residual TEST_ items, user_testaura01 remains FREE (no premium_until/premium_source/trial_used), usage collection empty. NEVER printed full base64 — only lengths and first 8 chars.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:622-637 compress_b64 correctly normalises any base64 image to a bounded JPEG (max 1024px, quality 72) with RGB conversion and thumbnail() (preserves aspect). Silent fallback returns the original b64 on decode failure — pragmatic (won't hard-fail on non-image blobs) but a malformed input would still be stored as-is. Not a bug but worth noting.
server.py:643-644 POST /api/items applies compress_b64 to BOTH photo and worn_photo before insert — verified end-to-end (input 746KB → stored 68KB, 11x reduction).
server.py:689-692 PUT /api/items/{id} guards each field with `if 'photo' in updates` before compressing — correct partial-update semantics; unrelated fields aren't touched.

server.py:756 _clean_photo output is passed through compress_b64 before return, so /api/capture.clean_image is guaranteed bounded (observed 34,424 chars vs the reported pre-fix ~460KB) — this is the specific vector called out in the bug report.

server.py:636-637 The except swallows all Pillow errors silently. If Pillow ever fails on a valid image (e.g. HEIC without pillow-heif), oversized blobs could still slip through. Consider logging the exception at WARNING for future forensics.
compress_b64 is idempotent and safe on already-small images (JPEG re-encode at q=72 of a 26KB image stays ~similar); no risk of visible quality regression across repeated PUTs beyond the first.

Threshold sanity: the request spec says 'stored photo < ~200KB base64'. Real photographic content easily fits (68KB observed). High-entropy synthetic noise imagery can exceed 200KB even after compression — not a real-world case for wardrobe photos.

rca_of_issue: RCA of the original bug (already fixed by main agent): the wardrobe grid renders items as base64 <Image src='data:image/jpeg;base64,...'/>. Overly large base64 strings (~460KB from /api/capture Gemini output, and some raw camera uploads) either failed to render on-device or were dropped by an intermediate decoder, showing blank tiles. Fix normalises every stored photo through Pillow (thumbnail 1024px + JPEG q=72), keeping typical wardrobe photos ≤ ~100KB base64 and guaranteed valid JPEG. Verified across create/update/capture paths and confirmed no oversized photos remain in the DB.
